All writes are scoped to the task's storage anchor (the owning user's file tree for development runs, the task's team subtree for deployed runs), resolved automatically from the running task. For each persisted file a JSON reference {path, url?} is emitted on the json lane; the signed url is included when 'Emit download URL' is enabled.

Leave it on 'Write under a new name' unless you are deliberately re-running into the same directory.

image_orient.description: Turns scanned photographs the right way up. Finds faces at each of the four right-angle rotations and keeps the one they agree on, so a print scanned sideways or upside down comes out upright. It only acts when the evidence is clear: anything it is unsure about is passed through untouched and listed on the text lane, because a photo turned the wrong way is worse than one left alone.

image_orient.confidenceWeight.description: When one rotation shows a bigger face but another shows a clearer one, this decides which wins. 'Balanced' is the safe default: measured over 98 album photographs it corrected 37 and got none wrong. Raising it rescues photos where an upside-down face is detected with a larger box than the upright one - but it acts on thinner evidence, and at the highest setting with 'Faces needed to decide' at 1 it corrected 39 and got 3 wrong. Raise it only if upside-down photos are being missed, and check the results.
image_orient.confidenceWeight.title: Face clarity vs face size

image_orient.detectSize.description: How big a copy of the photo the face search runs on. Your image is never scaled - this only affects the search. Raise it if faces in group photos are being missed; the cost grows with the square, so 1600 is about four times the work of 800.
image_orient.detectSize.title: Detection size (px)

image_orient.margin.description: How clearly the winning orientation must beat the next best one. Measured over 98 real album photographs, 'Balanced' corrected 37 and got none wrong. Move up if a photo ever comes out the wrong way round; move down only if you would rather fix more and check the results yourself.
image_orient.margin.title: How sure before rotating

image_orient.minConfidence.description: How certain the detector must be that something is a face before it gets a say. Raising it ignores doubtful faces; lowering it lets more in, including things that are not faces at all.
image_orient.minConfidence.title: Minimum face score

image_orient.minFaces.description: How many faces must agree before the photo is turned. One face is thin evidence and was behind most of the mistakes in testing, so two is the default. Lower to 1 for portraits and single-subject photos, where there is only ever one face to find.
image_orient.minFaces.title: Faces needed to decide

image_orient.quality.description: Type 'auto' to save at the same quality the photo already had, or a number from 1 to 100. Leave it on 'auto': the image has been through JPEG once already, so saving higher only makes the file bigger without recovering anything. Ignored for PNG, which is lossless. Photos that are not rotated are never re-saved at all.

normalize_facts.description:
A deterministic fact normalizer for the audit-grade financial extraction suite. Reads facts on the answers lane and cleans them with pure Python (no LLM): it parses numbers and signs (parentheses, trailing/unicode minus, thousands separators), detects and tags currency and scale (never converting, never multiplying the value), maps free-text labels to standard metric names, and de-duplicates identical facts.

The normalization is non-destructive: the raw label and value are kept, a normalized block is added, and a provenance entry records how each field was derived. Currency is tagged, not converted — conversion is the separate currency_convert_explicit node. Records that are not fact objects pass through unchanged.

scan_cropper.description: Splits a scan that holds several photos - a photo album page, or a handful of prints laid on the platen - into one image per photo. It works out what the background is from the scan itself, so there is no white/dark/album mode to choose, straightens each photo, and cuts apart prints mounted edge to edge. Detection runs on a downscaled copy and the crops are taken at full resolution.

scan_cropper.album.tune.description: Reveals every value this scan type uses, filled in with its own numbers, so you can start from it and adjust one thing rather than setting all ten from scratch.
scan_cropper.album.tune.title: Show advanced settings

scan_cropper.deskew.description: Rotates each photo upright as it is cut, so a slightly crooked scan comes out square. Turn this off only if you would rather keep the original pixels untouched - the photo then keeps its tilt and has page-coloured wedges in the corners.
scan_cropper.deskew.title: Straighten photos

scan_cropper.detail.detectSize.description: How big a copy of the scan the search for photos runs on. Your crops are always cut from the full-resolution original, so this only trades speed against how precisely photo edges are located. It is the main speed control and the cost is quadratic: 3000 to 2000 is about 2.25x faster. Raise it if crop edges land slightly inside or outside the photo.
scan_cropper.detail.detectSize.title: Detection size (px)

scan_cropper.detail.maxDepth.description: Photos mounted edge to edge look like one shape and have to be cut apart; this is how many times a shape may be cut. Set to 0 when your photos never touch - it switches off the most expensive part of the search and is by far the biggest speed win. Raise it if a row of several touching photos comes out as one image.
scan_cropper.detail.maxDepth.title: Separate touching photos

scan_cropper.detail.tune.description: Reveals every value this scan type uses, filled in with its own numbers, so you can start from it and adjust one thing rather than setting all ten from scratch.
scan_cropper.detail.tune.title: Show advanced settings

scan_cropper.detectSize.description: How big a copy of the scan the search for photos runs on. Your crops are always cut from the full-resolution original, so this only trades speed against how precisely photo edges are located. It is the main speed control and the cost is quadratic: 3000 to 2000 is about 2.25x faster. Raise it if crop edges land slightly inside or outside the photo.
scan_cropper.detectSize.title: Detection size (px)

scan_cropper.loose.maxDepth.description: Photos mounted edge to edge look like one shape and have to be cut apart; this is how many times a shape may be cut. Set to 0 when your photos never touch - it switches off the most expensive part of the search and is by far the biggest speed win. Raise it if a row of several touching photos comes out as one image.
scan_cropper.loose.maxDepth.title: Separate touching photos

scan_cropper.loose.minRelative.description: Throws away finds much smaller than the biggest photo on the page, on the assumption they are torn-off pieces of one photo rather than photos in their own right. 0.4 means 'drop anything under 40% of the largest'. Lower it, or set 0 to keep everything, when one page genuinely holds photos of very different sizes.

scan_cropper.loose.tune.description: Reveals every value this scan type uses, filled in with its own numbers, so you can start from it and adjust one thing rather than setting all ten from scratch.
scan_cropper.loose.tune.title: Show advanced settings

scan_cropper.maxArea.description: Ignore anything larger than this share of the whole scan. Kept below 1.0 so that failing to find the photos returns nothing rather than handing you the entire page as one giant 'photo'. You rarely need to change this.
scan_cropper.maxArea.title: Largest photo to keep

scan_cropper.maxAspect.description: How stretched a rectangle may be before it is rejected as not a photo, measured as long side divided by short side. 5.0 comfortably allows panoramas. Lower it if strips of page edge or scanner lid are being picked up as photos.
scan_cropper.maxAspect.title: Longest allowed shape

scan_cropper.maxDepth.description: Photos mounted edge to edge look like one shape and have to be cut apart; this is how many times a shape may be cut. Set to 0 when your photos never touch - it switches off the most expensive part of the search and is by far the biggest speed win. Raise it if a row of several touching photos comes out as one image.
scan_cropper.maxDepth.title: Separate touching photos

scan_cropper.minArea.description: Ignore anything smaller than this share of the whole scan. 0.005 means half a percent of the page. Lower it if small photos or stamps are being missed; raise it if specks and dust are coming out as tiny crops.
scan_cropper.minArea.title: Smallest photo to keep

scan_cropper.minRelative.description: Throws away finds much smaller than the biggest photo on the page, on the assumption they are torn-off pieces of one photo rather than photos in their own right. 0.4 means 'drop anything under 40% of the largest'. Lower it, or set 0 to keep everything, when one page genuinely holds photos of very different sizes.
scan_cropper.minRelative.title: Discard small leftovers

scan_cropper.profile.description: Pick what you actually scanned and nothing else needs setting. There is no white/dark/album background choice because the node works the background out from the scan itself - what these change is whether photos touch each other, how similar their sizes are, and how grainy the page is. Every scan type carries a 'Show advanced settings' switch that opens up its own values for tweaking.
scan_cropper.profile.title: Scan type

scan_cropper.quality.description: Type 'auto' to match the quality your scanner saved at, or a number from 1 to 100. Leave it on 'auto': saving above the original cannot recover detail the scanner already threw away, it only makes files bigger - a quality-75 scan re-saved at 100 is roughly four times the size and looks the same.
scan_cropper.quality.title: JPEG quality

scan_cropper.qualityTolerance.description: Only used when JPEG quality is 'auto'. How much final quality to give up in exchange for smaller files. 0.2 keeps files large and near-perfect, 1.0 makes them roughly half the size with a difference you would struggle to see. Measured on a 33-page album: 657 MB at 0.2, 463 MB at 0.5, 330 MB at 1.0.
scan_cropper.qualityTolerance.title: File size vs quality (dB)

scan_cropper.ratioTolerance.description: Used only when deciding whether a shape is two touching photos or one whole photo: how far the pieces may sit from a standard print shape (6x4, 5x7, square and so on). It never rejects a photo on its own, so an unusual shape is still kept. Raise it if photos that should be split are staying joined; lower it if one photo is being cut in half.
scan_cropper.ratioTolerance.title: Print shape tolerance (%)

scan_cropper.skew.description: How crooked the join between two touching photos may be and still be found. NOT a speed setting - lowering it narrows the search without saving any time, because the number of angles tried does not drop below five. Raise it only if touching photos on a visibly crooked scan are not being separated.
scan_cropper.skew.title: Tilt allowance when separating (degrees)

scan_cropper.texture.description: How smooth an area has to be before it counts as empty page rather than part of a photo. RAISE this if the page itself is being detected as photos (grainy, patterned or fabric-covered pages). LOWER it if a photo with large flat areas - a plain sky, a studio backdrop - is being cut short or missed.

scan_cropper.textured.texture.description: How smooth an area has to be before it counts as empty page rather than part of a photo. schema_validate.description:
A guard node for the audit-grade financial extraction suite. It flags inconsistencies in structured facts — most notably a cost row stored as revenue (and other metric/category mismatches, sign-convention violations, and missing amounts/currency) — and makes sure provenance is never dropped. Reads and writes the answers lane.

Validation is non-destructive: original fields are kept, a validation block (valid, severity, flags) is added, and a provenance entry records that the fact was checked. Records that are not fact objects pass through unchanged; nothing is ever dropped or fixed.

schema_validate.category_field.title: Category field

schema_validate.category_metric_map.description: Map of canonical category to metric keyword substrings that imply it. Drives the cost-as-revenue check. Leave unset to use the built-in map covering revenue, expense, asset, and liability; set an explicit empty map to disable the metric/category mismatch check.
schema_validate.category_metric_map.title: Category → metric keywords

http_request.maxConcurrentRequests.description: Maximum number of HTTP requests that can be in-flight simultaneously.

http_request.urlWhitelist.description: Python regex patterns applied with match() to the final canonical URL after path substitution, regular query parameters, and query-based API-key auth. A request-time source recognizer accepts only exact literal/escaped hosts with supported numeric-port forms, or a deliberate [^/] whole-authority form, followed by an explicit authority boundary. Unsupported or ambiguous authority syntax fails closed even when the regex matches. [] or only blank placeholder rows allows all public destinations; non-public destinations remain blocked. Blank rows mixed with valid patterns are ignored; invalid non-empty regexes, non-string values, and malformed entries fail closed.
http_request.urlWhitelist.title: URL Whitelist

http_request.whitelistPattern.description: Applied with Python regex match() to the final canonical URL after path substitution, regular query parameters, and query-based API-key auth. After matching, a fail-closed source grammar requires a literal HTTP(S) scheme; an exact literal/escaped DNS, IPv4, or bracketed-IPv6 host with an optional exact or [0-9]-based port policy, or a whole-authority [^/] policy; and an explicit path, query, or end boundary. Unsupported or ambiguous authority regex syntax is denied at request time. Example: ^https://api\.example\.com(?::[0-9]+)?(?:/|$). Scheme-only prefixes are denied; use an empty whitelist to allow all public destinations. Blank placeholder rows are ignored.
http_request.whitelistPattern.title: URL Pattern (regex)

tool_http_request.title: HTTP Request

laserdata.cloud.connection_string.description: LaserData Cloud endpoint in the form user:password@host:port — the user and password from your deployment's Credentials tab, the domain and TCP port from its Overview tab. TLS is automatic for *.laserdata.cloud hosts (the SDK ships the LaserData root CA). The deployment must serve VSR — created on/after 2026-07-31; recreate older ones. Falls back to the LASER_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable when blank.
laserdata.cloud.connection_string.title: Connection string

laserdata.folded.description: When on (default), 'recall' folds the durable memory topic in-process — works against plain Apache Iggy and LaserData Cloud alike (verified live). Turn off only to read a managed KV view on a deployment that serves one.
laserdata.folded.title: Folded recall

laserdata.local.connection_string.description: Apache Iggy connection string in the form user:password@host:port, e.g. iggy:iggy@localhost:8090. The server must be a VSR-enabled Iggy build — use laser-stack (its ./scripts/up prints a ready connection string); stock pre-VSR Iggy images cannot talk to this SDK. A containerized engine needs an address reachable from the container, e.g. host.docker.internal. Falls back to the LASER_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable when blank.
laserdata.local.connection_string.title: Connection string

laserdata.namespace.description: The memory scope every call reads and writes, e.g. customer:42. The agent can pass a namespace per call; a namespace is required on the call or here.
laserdata.namespace.title: Namespace

laserdata.op_timeout.description: Max seconds any single memory operation (including the first connect) may take before it fails.
laserdata.op_timeout.title: Operation timeout (s)

laserdata.recall_limit.description: Maximum number of memory items to retrieve per recall.
laserdata.recall_limit.title: Recall limit

laserdata.show_advanced.description: Show advanced options. The defaults work for most cases, leave off for a simple setup.
laserdata.show_advanced.title: Advanced settings

laserdata.stream.description: The Iggy stream the memory topics live in, pinned as the connection's default stream. All nodes sharing one memory must use the same stream.
laserdata.stream.title: Stream

tool_laserdata_memory.title: LaserData Memory

tool_mem0.description: Long-term, shared agent memory exposed as tools, backed by the hosted Mem0 Platform. Exposes two agent tools: 'remember' stores conversation turns and 'recall' returns the relevant memories. Set your API key and a user id and it works; point several agents at the same project (and ids) to share one memory.

mem0.agent_id.description: Optional agent scope. Caution: on the hosted Mem0 platform an agent_id is not reliably stored on the memory but still narrows recall, so setting it can make recalls come back empty. Prefer scoping by user id; leave this empty unless you have verified it works.
mem0.agent_id.title: Agent id

mem0.api_key.description: Mem0 Platform API key (m0-...). Get it from the Mem0 dashboard: app.mem0.ai → API Keys.
mem0.api_key.title: API Key

mem0.app_id.description: Optional app scope. Same caveat as Agent id: it narrows recall but is not reliably stored on the hosted platform, so setting it can hide memories. Prefer scoping by user id.
mem0.app_id.title: App id

mem0.base_url.description: Mem0 REST API base URL. Defaults to the hosted endpoint; override for self-hosted / enterprise deployments.
mem0.base_url.title: Base URL

mem0.infer.description: When on (default), Mem0 runs LLM extraction to derive salient facts from the turns. When off, the raw messages are stored verbatim.
mem0.infer.title: Infer memories

mem0.ingest_timeout.description: Max seconds 'remember' waits/polls for background extraction to finish before returning a 'queued' result.
mem0.ingest_timeout.title: Store timeout (s)

mem0.run_id.description: Optional session/run scope stamped on stored memories and used to narrow recall. Can be passed by the agent per call.
mem0.run_id.title: Run id

mem0.search_limit.description: Maximum number of memory rows to retrieve per recall.
mem0.search_limit.title: Recall limit

mem0.show_advanced.description: Show advanced options. The defaults work for most cases, leave off for a simple setup.
mem0.show_advanced.title: Advanced settings

mem0.user_id.description: Who this memory belongs to (used to store and recall). Can be passed by the agent per call. At least one scope (user id, or an advanced agent/run/app id) is required.
mem0.user_id.title: User id

mem0.wait.description: When on (default), 'remember' polls Mem0 until background extraction finishes, so a following 'recall' can see the new memory. When off, 'remember' returns immediately and extraction runs in the background.
mem0.wait.title: Synchronous store

tool_mem0.title: Mem0

tool_n8n.description: Trigger n8n workflows from a RocketRide pipeline or an agent. As a pipeline step, lane input is POSTed to a workflow's webhook and the response flows downstream; as a tool, an agent can trigger workflows and inspect workflows/executions. Self-hosted: configure the n8n base URL and (for listing/polling) a public API key.

tool_n8n.apiKey.description: n8n public API key. Needed only to list/inspect workflows and poll executions — not for triggering webhooks.
tool_n8n.apiKey.title: API Key (X-N8N-API-KEY)

tool_n8n.asyncTimeout.description: Max seconds to wait for an async execution to finish before raising an error.
tool_n8n.asyncTimeout.title: Execution timeout (seconds)

tool_n8n.baseUrl.description: Base URL of your n8n instance, e.g. http://localhost:5678 or https://n8n.example.com. If RocketRide runs in Docker, use http://host.docker.internal:5678 (or the n8n container name) — 'localhost' would point at the container.
tool_n8n.baseUrl.title: n8n Base URL

tool_n8n.mode.description: Sync requires the workflow to end in a 'Respond to Webhook' node. Async polls the execution via the public API (API key required).
tool_n8n.mode.title: Result mode

tool_n8n.payloadMode.description: How lane input is sent to the workflow. 'structured' preserves document boundaries + metadata; 'simple' (default) flattens to a single string for back-compat.
tool_n8n.payloadMode.title: Payload shape (pipeline step)

tool_n8n.readOnly.description: When ON, write operations (activate/deactivate workflow) are blocked.
tool_n8n.readOnly.title: Read-only mode

tool_n8n.syncTimeout.description: Max seconds to wait for the webhook response in sync mode (raise for slow workflows).
tool_n8n.syncTimeout.title: Response timeout (seconds)

tool_n8n.verifyTls.description: Leave ON. Disable only for a self-signed local n8n served over HTTPS.
tool_n8n.verifyTls.title: Verify TLS certificate

tool_n8n.webhookAuth.description: Authentication on the workflow's Webhook node. Separate from the API key above.
tool_n8n.webhookAuth.title: Webhook auth

tool_n8n.webhookHeaderName.description: Header name (when Webhook auth = Header auth).
tool_n8n.webhookHeaderName.title: Header name

tool_n8n.webhookHeaderValue.description: Header value (when Webhook auth = Header auth).
tool_n8n.webhookHeaderValue.title: Header value

tool_n8n.webhookToken.description: Token sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (when Webhook auth = Bearer token or JWT).
tool_n8n.webhookToken.title: Token

tool_n8n.workflow.description: The webhook path the target workflow listens on (set on its Webhook node). Used by the pipeline step and as the default for the trigger tool.
tool_n8n.workflow.title: Workflow (webhook path)

tool_n8n.title: n8n

tool_notion.description: Exposes a Notion workspace (search, pages, databases) as agent tools. Search, read, and write Notion pages and databases using an internal integration secret — search by title, query database rows, read a page's body as plain text, and create/update/append pages.
tool_notion.title: Notion

tool_onedrive.description: Exposes Microsoft OneDrive operations as agent tools. List and search files and folders, read metadata, download and upload content, create folders, copy/move/rename items, trash and restore, and manage sharing (links and permission grants) on the acting user's OneDrive via the Microsoft Graph drive API. Anonymous sharing links, invites to non-individual recipients, and permanent delete, are gated behind explicit config flags. Authenticates via an Entra app (client credentials) or user OAuth.

onedrive.access.description: Graph scopes to request. readonly: list, search, read metadata, and download only. write: full read/write (upload, create folders, copy/move/rename, trash/restore, and sharing).
onedrive.access.title: Access level

onedrive.allowHardDelete.description: Off by default. When off, only trash/restore are available; permanent delete is refused.
onedrive.allowHardDelete.title: Allow permanent delete

onedrive.allowPublicSharing.description: Off by default. When off, create_sharing_link refuses 'anonymous' links and invite only accepts recipients that resolve to individual directory users (distribution lists and unresolvable addresses are refused). Turn on to allow public links and unrestricted invites.
onedrive.allowPublicSharing.title: Allow public / org-wide sharing

tool_onedrive.title: OneDrive

tool_oura.description: Exposes Oura Ring health data as read-only agent tools. Covers daily sleep, readiness, activity, stress, resilience, SpO2, heart rate, workouts, sessions, tags, VO2 max, cardiovascular age, battery level, and personal info.

oura.token.description: Oura API bearer token: an OAuth2 access token from a registered app at cloud.ouraring.com (personal access tokens were deprecated in Dec 2025; previously issued ones still work). Grants read-only access to the token owner's data. Falls back to the ROCKETRIDE_OURA_TOKEN environment variable when empty.
oura.token.title: Access Token

tool_oura.title: Oura

tool_outlook_calendar.description: Exposes Microsoft Outlook Calendar operations as agent tools. List and read events (including calendarView expansion of recurrences), create/update/delete events, respond to invitations, find meeting times, get free/busy schedules, list and create calendars, and delta-sync a calendar view, on the acting user's calendar via the Microsoft Graph calendar API. Authenticates via an Entra app (client credentials) or user OAuth.

outlook_calendar.access.description: Graph scopes to request. readonly: list and read events/calendars, find meeting times, get schedules, and delta-sync only. write: full read/write (default) — create/update/delete events, respond to invitations, and create calendars.
outlook_calendar.access.title: Access level

tool_outlook_calendar.title: Outlook Calendar

tool_outlook_mail.description: Exposes Microsoft Outlook Mail operations as agent tools. List, search, and read messages, send mail and replies/forwards, manage drafts, move/organize messages and folders, manage attachments, and mark read state, on the acting user's mailbox via the Microsoft Graph mail API. Sending requires the send or modify tier; drafts, moves, and other mutations require the modify tier; permanent delete is additionally gated behind an explicit config flag. Authenticates via an Entra app (client credentials) or user OAuth.

outlook_mail.access.description: Graph scopes to request. readonly: list, search, and read messages/folders/attachments only. send: readonly plus sending mail, replies, and forwards. modify: full read/write (default) — drafts, moves, organizing, attachments, and permanent delete (when allowHardDelete is on), plus send.
outlook_mail.access.title: Access level

outlook_mail.allowHardDelete.description: Off by default. When off, delete moves messages to Deleted Items; permanent delete is refused. Turn on to allow permanent delete.
outlook_mail.allowHardDelete.title: Allow permanent delete

tool_outlook_mail.title: Outlook Mail

tool_pipe.description: Exposes an inline pipeline as an agent tool. Connect this node's output lanes to any pipeline nodes on the same canvas. When an agent calls the tool, the input is routed to every connected output lane. End each connected branch with a response node to return results.

tool_pipe.return_type.description: Which response lane value to return to the agent
tool_pipe.return_type.title: Return Type

tool_pipe.tool_description.description: Natural-language description the agent uses to decide when to call this tool
tool_pipe.tool_description.title: Tool Description

tool_pipe.title: Pipeline Tool

tool_pipedrive.description: Exposes the Pipedrive CRM REST API v1 as agent tools. Covers deals, persons, organizations, activities, pipelines, stages, notes, leads, products, files, users, teams, goals, projects, and every other v1 resource.

pipedrive.allowRawRequest.description: Publishes the generic request tool, which can call any Pipedrive v1 endpoint by method and path. It uses the same authentication, rate-limit handling and read-only enforcement as the typed tools. Disable to restrict the agent to the typed tools only.
pipedrive.allowRawRequest.title: Allow raw API requests

pipedrive.apiToken.description: Pipedrive API token (Settings -> Personal preferences -> API), or an OAuth access token. Tokens starting with a JWT-style prefix are sent as a Bearer header; everything else is sent as the api_token query parameter.
pipedrive.apiToken.title: API Token

pipedrive.companyDomain.description: Your Pipedrive company domain, i.e. the "acme" in https://acme.pipedrive.com. When set, requests go to https://{domain}.pipedrive.com/api/v1; otherwise https://api.pipedrive.com/api/v1 is used.
pipedrive.companyDomain.title: Company Domain

pipedrive.readOnly.description: When enabled, every create, update and delete tool is blocked, and the generic request tool only accepts GET. Safe for agents that should only inspect the CRM.
pipedrive.readOnly.title: Read-only mode

pipedrive.toolGroups.description: Which groups of Pipedrive tools this node publishes to the agent. The full API is 255 tools, which is more than an LLM can choose between reliably, so only the selected groups are exposed. Pick one or more from the list; tool counts are shown per group, and selections totalling more than 120 log a warning but still run. Selecting All groups publishes everything and skips that warning.

enum: All groups (255) - skips the size warning

pipedrive.toolGroups.title: Tool groups

tool_pipedrive.title: Pipedrive

tool_python.description: Executes Python code in a restricted in-process sandbox via exec(). Only whitelisted modules can be imported. Dangerous builtins are removed.

tool_python.allowedModules.description: Modules the agent is allowed to import, in addition to the built-in defaults (math, json, re, collections, datetime, etc.).
tool_python.allowedModules.title: Additional Allowed Modules

tool_python.timeout.description: Maximum seconds a script may run before it is killed. Useful for long-running operations like network scans. Default is 20s, max is 1200s.
tool_python.timeout.title: Execution timeout (seconds)

tool_python.title: Python

tool_sheets.description: Exposes Google Sheets operations as agent tools. Read, write, append, and clear cell values; create spreadsheets; add, delete, duplicate, and copy sheets; and run arbitrary batchUpdate requests (formatting, charts, conditional formatting). Authenticates via a Google service account or user OAuth.

sheets.access.description: Sheets scopes to request. readonly: read values and metadata only. write: full read/write (create, update, append, clear, and structure changes such as add/delete/duplicate sheet).
sheets.access.title: Access level

tool_sheets.title: Google Sheets

tool_slack.description: Exposes Slack workspace operations as agent tools. Post messages to channels or threads, list public channels, read channel history, and verify the connection. Authenticates with a bot token, or an incoming-webhook URL for zero-scope post-only setups.

slack.token.description: Slack bot token (starts with xoxb-) from your app's OAuth & Permissions page. Needs chat:write to post, channels:read to list channels, and channels:history to read history. Leave empty when using a webhook URL.
slack.token.title: Bot User OAuth Token

slack.webhookUrl.description: Slack incoming-webhook URL for zero-scope setups. Enables ONLY message_post, and messages always go to the channel the webhook was created for. Configure either this or a bot token, not both.
slack.webhookUrl.title: Incoming Webhook URL

tool_slack.title: Slack

tool_tavily.description: Exposes Tavily real-time web search as an agent tool. Performs live web searches via the Tavily API and returns structured results with titles, URLs, content snippets, and relevance scores.

tool_tavily.maxResults.description: Maximum number of search results to return (1-20)
tool_tavily.maxResults.title: Max Results

tool_tavily.title: Tavily

tool_v0.description: A component that connects to Vercel's v0 API to generate React + Tailwind CSS UI components from natural-language prompts. Supports generate_ui (create a new component from a description) and refine_ui (iterate on a previous generation with follow-up instructions). Experimental: API availability and behavior may change.
tool_v0.title: v0 by Vercel

tool_vertex_search.description: A processing component that interacts with Google Vertex AI Vector Search.

vertex.deployedIndexId.description: The ID of the deployed index.
vertex.deployedIndexId.title: Deployed Index ID

vertex.indexEndpointId.description: The ID of the Vector Search Index Endpoint.
vertex.indexEndpointId.title: Index Endpoint ID

vertex.location.description: The Google Cloud region, e.g. us-central1.
vertex.location.title: Location

tool_vertex_search.title: Vertex AI Vector Search

tool_word.description: Exposes Microsoft Word document operations as agent tools. Read text, create documents from paragraph lists, append text, find/replace text, and export to PDF. Operates on docx files in the acting user's OneDrive via the Microsoft Graph drive content API, round-tripping through python-docx. Authenticates via an Entra app (client credentials) or user OAuth.

word.access.description: Graph scopes to request. readonly: read document text only. write: full read/write (create, append, replace text, export PDF).
word.access.title: Access level

tool_word.title: Word

tool_xtrace_memory.description: Long-term, shared agent memory exposed as tools, backed by xTrace Memory Manager. Exposes two agent tools: 'remember' stores conversation turns and 'recall' returns the relevant, ready-to-inject context. Set your API key and org id and it works; point several agents at the same org (and group) to share one memory.

xtrace_memory.agent_id.description: Optional agent scope stamped on ingested memories and AND-narrowed on recall.
xtrace_memory.agent_id.title: Agent id

xtrace_memory.api_key.description: xTrace API key (xtk_...). Get it from the Developer Portal: app.xtrace.ai → Settings → API Keys (not in mem.xtrace.ai).
xtrace_memory.api_key.title: API Key

xtrace_memory.app_id.description: Optional app scope stamped on ingested memories and AND-narrowed on recall.
xtrace_memory.app_id.title: App id

xtrace_memory.base_url.description: xTrace Memory API base URL. Production by default; use https://api.staging.xtrace.ai for staging.
xtrace_memory.base_url.title: Base URL

xtrace_memory.extract_artifacts.description: Opt into artifact extraction (the most expensive stage). Facts and episodes are always extracted. Leave off unless you need it.
xtrace_memory.extract_artifacts.title: Extract artifacts

xtrace_memory.group_ids.description: Optional. Comma-separated group ids (grp_...) to share memory across users/agents. Leave empty for private memory.
xtrace_memory.group_ids.title: Group ids (shared memory)

xtrace_memory.ingest_timeout.description: Max seconds to wait/poll for an ingest job to reach a terminal state.
xtrace_memory.ingest_timeout.title: Ingest timeout (s)

xtrace_memory.org_id.description: xTrace organization id (org_...). Same place as the API key: app.xtrace.ai → Settings → API Keys.
xtrace_memory.org_id.title: Org id

xtrace_memory.search_limit.description: Maximum number of memory rows to retrieve per recall.
xtrace_memory.search_limit.title: Recall limit

xtrace_memory.search_mode.description: 'compose' returns a ready-to-inject markdown context block (LLM-selected); 'retrieve' returns ranked rows only.
xtrace_memory.search_mode.title: Recall mode

xtrace_memory.show_advanced.description: Show advanced options. The defaults work for most cases, leave off for a simple setup.
xtrace_memory.show_advanced.title: Advanced settings

xtrace_memory.user_id.description: Who this memory belongs to (used to store and recall). Can be passed by the agent per call.
xtrace_memory.user_id.title: User id

xtrace_memory.wait.description: When on, ingest waits (up to ~30s) for extraction to finish so the agent gets a terminal result. When off, ingest returns immediately and runs in the background.
xtrace_memory.wait.title: Synchronous ingest

tool_xtrace_memory.title: xTrace Memory

tools.description: A source component that transfers no data: it exists to host tool nodes. Connect tools to it via the tool invoke channel and call them directly from a client with client.tool() - no agent, no LLM, no data lanes. Ideal for pipelines whose whole purpose is exposing capabilities (file storage, vector store management, integrations) to an application.
tools.title: Tools

tts_elevenlabs.description: Converts incoming text into speech using the ElevenLabs text-to-speech API. Calls the vendor API directly from the engine host over HTTPS and emits MP3 bytes on the audio lane. The model and voice lists are maintained manually; the API key falls back to the ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable when blank.
tts_elevenlabs.title: Text To Speech (ElevenLabs)

tts_openai.description: Converts incoming text into speech using the OpenAI text-to-speech API. Calls the vendor API directly from the engine host over HTTPS and emits MP3 bytes on the audio lane. Model and voice lists are maintained manually; the API key falls back to the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable when blank.

tts_openai.voice.description: OpenAI TTS voice. The newer voices (marin, cedar) require a GPT-4o TTS model.
tts_openai.voice.title: Voice

tts_openai.title: Text To Speech (OpenAI)

tts_rime.description: Converts incoming text into speech using the Rime text-to-speech API. Calls the vendor API directly from the engine host over HTTPS and emits MP3 bytes on the audio lane. Rime speakers are model-specific, so each model exposes its own curated speaker list; the API key falls back to the RIME_API_KEY environment variable when blank.

tts_rime.arcana.voice.description: Rime voice for the Arcana model.
tts_rime.arcana.voice.title: Speaker

tts_rime.coda.voice.description: Rime voice for the Coda model.
tts_rime.coda.voice.title: Speaker

tts_rime.mistv2.voice.description: Rime voice for the Mist v2 model.
tts_rime.mistv2.voice.title: Speaker

tts_rime.mistv3.voice.description: Rime voice for the Mist v3 model.
tts_rime.mistv3.voice.title: Speaker

tts_rime.title: Text To Speech (Rime)

twelvelabs.description: Sends a video to TwelveLabs along with instructions and returns the generated text response.

twelvelabs.instructions.description: Instructions to guide TwelveLabs when analyzing the video.
twelvelabs.instructions.title: Instructions

twelvelabs.title: TwelveLabs

vectorizer.description: An internal filter that chunks incoming text, computes embeddings via the configured embedding component, and writes the resulting documents to the vector store.
vectorizer.title: Vectorizer

video_composer.description: Stitches a sequence of image frames into an MP4 video using FFmpeg. Place after any image-producing filter to re-encode matched frames into a playable video clip.

composer.crf.description: Constant Rate Factor for H.264. Lower = better quality, larger file. Range 0-51.
composer.crf.title: Quality (CRF)

composer.fps.description: Playback speed of the output video. Should match the upstream frame rate.
composer.fps.title: Output frame rate (fps)

video_composer.title: Video Composer

weaviate.description: A component that stores vector embeddings in a Weaviate instance for semantic search and retrieval. It supports structured metadata and schema configuration, enabling efficient storage, indexing, and querying of high-dimensional data. Ideal for AI pipelines involving similarity search, recommendation systems, and knowledge management.

vector.cloud.host.description: Enter the server IP address e.g. <your-instance-name>.weaviate.cloud

weaviate.serverName.description: Namespace for agent-facing tool names, e.g. 'weaviate' exposes tools as weaviate.search / weaviate.upsert / weaviate.delete. Change this when running multiple Weaviate nodes in the same pipeline so their tool names do not collide.
weaviate.serverName.title: Tool Server Name

weaviate.title: Weaviate

webhook.description: A source component that listens for incoming HTTP requests and accepts uploaded documents or data from external systems or processes. It enables seamless integration for document ingestion, allowing external systems to trigger the component and send files for further processing. Configurable with endpoint and authentication settings, it ensures secure and reliable document transfer for pipeline processing. Ideal for receiving documents, images, or other files from external platforms via HTTP-based communication.
webhook.title: Webhook

zip.description: An internal target component that collects processed content and packages it into a ZIP archive available for export or download.
zip.title: ZIP Creation
